cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I can't open the cupboard. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Did making that room involve moving the sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put the things you'll need somewhere easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How thoughtful. Would those be the mugs in your sock drawer, or has someone else improved the kitchen too?

mechanism: A approves a benign-looking explanation while asking increasingly specific questions that draw out who rearranged the room and its contents.
confusable: A direct accusation would skip the Drive; questions should remain innocent in form while exposing actual alterations under A assumed authority.
comparison: Blocked cupboard and relocated mugs differ from the picnic calendar handwriting investigation.
seedUse: Use D40-b yoga rationale and helpful item relocation, with S01 permission converting explanations into further authorized inquiry.
